newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek cap mkts commission to question 10 brokers.
newsitem.headline: Greek cap mkts commission to question 10 brokers.

text.p: Greece's capital markets commission said it would question the 10 brokerages that were counterparties to trades with Delta Securities, charged last week with fraud, and ask them to explain their transactions.

Athens bourse members will be given until 0900 local time on Thursday, November 14, to fully settle their obligations with the clearing house both on cash and securities, the commission said in a statement.
All members that meet the commission's deadline would be admitted to the exchange for trading, it said.
The commission in cooperation with the bourse will ask international auditing firms to carry out audits of brokerages related to the Delta Securities scandal.
Earlier, a letter signed by bourse supervisor George Malakis named 10 member firms which were to be audited by state inspectors.

Athens stock exchange member Delta Securities, in the red with the bourse's clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas, was charged with extensive, repeated fraud last week. Its offices were sealed and assets frozen.
Delta has made no comment since the charges were brought.
The public prosecutor has also laid negligence charges against unnamed stock exchange officials and employees in a widening probe into the Delta scandal.
Aside from token trades by some bank brokerages on Tuesday amounting to less than 4.0 million drachmas, the Athens bourse has not traded for three days, still caught in an uproar.
Brokers have slammed the government for a possible cover up and were discussing their next move at their association's headquarters in yet another effort to resolve the crisis.
